sections.h2: Which Calloway County offices handle a Murray property tax bill?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work. The Property Valuation Administrator puts a value on the house, and the Sheriff's Office bills and collects. By the sheriff's own count, its tax desk processes over 27 thousand bills and more than 11 million dollars a year, so it is the main collector for Murray and the rural parts of the county alike.

Homestead and disability forms, and value questions, go to the PVA at 270-753-3482. Payments go to the tax office at 701 Olive Street. When the sheriff's season ends, delinquent bills pass to the county clerk, a hand-off the state revenue department describes step by step.

The county spans about 385 square miles of land on the state's southwest edge and held 37,103 people in 2020. Murray State University is in Murray, and with a large rental share the housing stock turns over differently here than in farm counties.

sections.h2: What does a late Calloway County tax payment cost?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 gives early payers 2% off, then charges face value until December 31 and penalties after that. Calloway's twist is the early cutoff: the sheriff's page says a payment postmarked by November 15 earns the discount, two weeks sooner than Caldwell County's November 30.

Your bill carries its own dated schedule in the top right corner, and the amount climbs with each later date. Past the discount, the statewide steps apply:

  • Mid-November through December 31: the printed amount, no extras.
  • Throughout January: a 5% penalty.
  • Starting February 1: a 10% penalty and a sheriff's add-on fee.

The sheriff accepts cash, check, money order or an online card payment. A returned check carries a $50 fee, and penalties can apply again when you resend. The office asks customers not to mail cash.

sections.h2: Where and how do I pay in Murray?
sections.html:
Four routes work: a drop box, the mail, the counter or the website. The box on the west side of the building at 701 Olive Street never closes. Counter service runs weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., and the bill must come with you.

  • By mail: send the stub and a check to 701 Olive St., Murray, KY 42071, and add a stamped return envelope to get a receipt back.
  • Online: the sheriff's tax search page ends with a printable receipt.
  • Several bills at once: allowed by mail or at the counter if every stub is enclosed.
  • Questions: the tax office answers at (270) 761-4TAX.

Pay just the one "balance due" figure for your date. The sheriff cautions against splitting the payment among the state, county and school lines on the bill.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax when a Calloway County house sells?
sections.html:
The sheriff's FAQ describes a standard split: the seller covers a prorated slice of the year at closing, and the buyer pays the whole bill once it is issued. When unsure, read the settlement statement.

A sale that closes before billing leaves the title company to hold back an estimate. Ask the tax office for today's balance and whether an older year is open, since past-due taxes are paid at the clerk, not the sheriff. Owners whose lender escrows still receive a copy of the bill, so they can see how the tax was figured.

The City of Murray lists property taxes on its online payments page too. Ask the city whether a bill is open on your parcel before choosing a closing date, and keep every receipt.

  • Request the sheriff's balance for the parcel.
  • Ask the clerk about any older delinquent year.
  • Check with the PVA that an exemption, if you have one, is on the account.
  • Hand the title company the bill number from your stub.

sections.h2: How can I contest a Calloway County value?
sections.html:
Speak with the PVA before anything else, then file with the clerk once the roll closes. Public inspection of the roll lasts 13 days from the first Monday in May, and a conference with the PVA must precede an appeal to the local board, per the state's property tax calendar.

Evidence decides these hearings. Expect the board to weigh land, buildings, rebuild cost and nearby sales. The state's sales comparison approach adjusts neighboring sales for differences like a basement, so collect three or four recent Murray sales and mark where your house differs.

An owner who files but fails to appear cannot take the case further, so attend with your paperwork. After the hearing the board must give a written reason for any increase or decrease, and you are allowed to make an audio recording.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can a Calloway County owner claim?
sections.html:
Owners who live in the home and are 65 or older, or totally disabled, may apply for the homestead exemption. The sheriff's page tells anyone who might qualify to call the PVA at 270-753-3482 rather than pay first.

Only one exemption is allowed per household, and it belongs to the owner instead of the property, so your buyer files a new form. Service-connected totally disabled veterans do not refile each year.

Under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution, farm acreage is valued on what it can produce, not on market price. That gap can be wide near town, so anyone selling acres should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

sections.h2: How does the Calloway County housing market compare?
sections.html:
A typical owner-occupied Calloway home is valued at $183,200 for 2020 to 2024, well over Caldwell County's $118,500. Owners live in just 63.9 percent of homes, and renters held 35.8 percent of occupied units in the 2020 count.

Household income in the county is $52,706 for 2020 to 2024, and 31.2 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher, against 17.1 percent in Caldwell County, a gap that fits a university town. Workers average 17.3 minutes getting to work, the shortest commute of the four counties in this group, so a house close to Murray's jobs and campus has a built-in appeal. The county makes up the Murray micropolitan area, and the 2020 Census put 15,108 households in it.

The county was created in 1822 from Hickman County, and a 1906 fire at the courthouse destroyed almost all of its early records, which is why old title questions sometimes need extra research. Landlords with a rental near campus, heirs with a house in Murray, and owners with a vacant farmhouse can sell as-is to a cash buyer. That route avoids waiting on a buyer's financing and the repair requests that follow an inspection. A signed offer still needs the tax payoff figures above, so collect them before you accept a closing date.

faqs.q: By when must I pay to get the Calloway County discount?
faqs.a: Payments postmarked by November 15 earn the 2% discount, according to the sheriff's page. The dated schedule on the bill is the final word.

faqs.q: Where is the sheriff's tax office in Murray?
faqs.a: 701 Olive Street. It serves weekdays until 4:30 p.m., and a drop box on the west side stays open all day and night. The phone is (270) 761-4TAX.

faqs.q: Does the sheriff take credit cards?
faqs.a: Yes, but the sheriff's page says credit cards are accepted only through its website. Cash, check and money order are also accepted, and cash should never go in the mail.

faqs.q: Who pays the bill if my Murray house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: Normally you pay a prorated share at closing and the buyer pays the full bill once issued. The settlement statement shows the split.

faqs.q: Must I fix up a Calloway County house first?
faqs.a: No, a cash buyer can take it as-is. Unpaid property tax is settled from the proceeds, so request payoff amounts from the sheriff and clerk first.
